question: Does the held-out deeper-hop transfer claim require RL on lower-hop instances (KG-Hopper-style), or does supervised fine-tuning on lower-hop instances with context-enriched supervision already transfer, making the RL stage unnecessary?
description: The deferred Stage-3 RL component is precedented as a strong performer (KG-Hopper reports a 7B RL-trained model outperforming much larger multi-step systems up to 70B on eight KG reasoning benchmarks), which raises the possibility that any deeper-hop transfer gain will come from the RL stage rather than from context supervision, or conversely that RL is unnecessary because supervised training on lower-hop instances already transfers. Which stage actually drives transfer is untested.
rationale: Determines whether the deferred RL stage is a necessary part of the investigation or an avoidable expense and confound; if supervised lower-hop training transfers, the pipeline simplifies to a single training method.
